growth_signal.value: Just announced a partnership with HeartBeat.bio to apply its 3D spatial mapping technology to heart disease research.

raised.value: €5.9M blended financing: €3.9M private capital led by Voima Ventures and Nordic Science Investments, plus a €2M non-dilutive EIC Transition grant

entry.idea: Cubase Bio maps where genes are active inside tissue in true 3D, instead of the flat 2D slices most tools use, giving drug researchers a much fuller picture of how disease develops inside an organ.
entry.lesson: A founding team with a proven prior exit in the same specific niche can raise funding and land partnerships quickly, even soon after emerging from stealth.
entry.name: Cubase Bio

growth.basis: substitute: the founders' prior spatial-biology company was acquired by 10x Genomics, and the company just landed a new research partnership right after emerging from stealth
growth.reason: No revenue or customer numbers are available yet, but the founders have a proven track record and are already signing partnerships.

market.reason: Spatial biology tools serve pharmaceutical and biotech research budgets worldwide, a real but specialised scientific tools market.

tech.reason: True 3D DNA-microscopy-based spatial transcriptomics is deep, novel biology and imaging science that would take competitors years to replicate.

sources.title: Sweden's Cubase Bio teams up with HeartBeat.bio to advance 3D spatial mapping for heart disease - ArcticStartup

entry.twist: Its founders previously built and sold a similar spatial biology company, Cartana, to 10x Genomics, where their technology became the foundation of a major commercial product line.
entry.who_pays: Pharmaceutical and biotech companies pay to use Cubase Bio's 3D tissue mapping technology to accelerate their drug discovery research, including new partnerships like its work with HeartBeat.bio on heart disease.
entry.why_now: Drug discovery increasingly depends on understanding disease in realistic, three-dimensional tissue structures like organoids, which flat 2D imaging tools cannot properly capture.

mentions.snippet: Maps biological tissue in true 3D for drug discovery; partnering on heart disease.
